title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E410 first derives the equilibrium equations of a perfectly flexible or elastic filament (planar) in intrinsic form. The arc length is s and Φ is the angle with dx/ds = sinΦ and dy/ds = cosΦ. T is the tension along the tangent MT and V the normal (shear) force; v is the moment arm, so Vv is the bending moment. The applied loads per unit length are p (tangential) and q (normal, along mr). The equilibrium equations are dT/ds + V dΦ/ds = p and dV/ds − T dΦ/ds = q, together with the moment relations. In §§XXXVI–XXXVIII Euler turns the dynamic problem into a static one by d'Alembert's principle. An element of weight Σds needs the 'forces required to produce the motion', (Σds/2g)(∂²x/∂t², ∂²y/∂t²), in directions AX and XM; the 2g factor reflects Euler's units, with g the fall height in one second. The applied forces must be equivalent to these required forces, so the required forces applied in reverse (directions XA and MX) are in equilibrium with the applied forces at each instant.

On this page he resolves the reversed inertial force (F_x, F_y) = (Σds/2g)(x_tt, y_tt) into components. Tangential: F_x sinΦ + F_y cosΦ. Normal (along mr): F_y sinΦ − F_x cosΦ. The effective tangential and normal loads are therefore p ds + (Σds/2g)(x_tt sinΦ + y_tt cosΦ) and q ds + (Σds/2g)(y_tt sinΦ − x_tt cosΦ). These replace p ds and q ds in the static equations.

In §XXXIX the applied loads are instead given in Cartesian form: P ds along XA and Q ds along MX. Projecting gives tangential load ds[(P + Σx_tt/2g) sinΦ + (Q + Σy_tt/2g) cosΦ] and normal load ds[(Q + Σy_tt/2g) sinΦ − (P + Σx_tt/2g) cosΦ].

In §XL (next page) these combine into the PDE system of the moving elastic filament. The unknowns T, V, Φ are now functions of (s, t), so partial-derivative brackets are introduced; the resulting system is the planar Kirchhoff-type rod equations in intrinsic form with d'Alembert inertia terms.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The projection formulas are consistent with dx/ds = sinΦ and dy/ds = cosΦ.
Sign convention check: the inertial terms enter with + because they are applied in the reversed directions XA and MX. These are the same directions in which P and Q act, so adding them is consistent.

Previous-page transcription: 'vim in directione XA = Σds/2g (ddy/dt²)' should read ddx/dt² for direction XA (the ddy component goes along MX). This is a printing or transcription slip outside this page.

ideas.what: Reducing the motion of a continuous filament to instantaneous equilibrium by applying the reversed 'forces required to produce the motion' to each element.
ideas.usually_credited_to: d'Alembert (Traité de dynamique, 1743); used systematically by Euler
ideas.where_published: Many Euler papers; E410 itself (Novi Comm. 15, 1771); discussed by Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11 part 2)

ideas.what: Projecting Cartesian load and inertia components onto the tangent and normal of the deformed filament, to feed intrinsic equilibrium equations.
ideas.modern_name: Frenet-type intrinsic (tangential/normal) decomposition of balance of linear momentum for a rod
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (intrinsic string/rod equations); later Kirchhoff, Clebsch for rods
ideas.where_published: E410; earlier E318/E319-era string papers; Truesdell 1960 account

ideas.what: Resulting general PDE system for the planar motion of an elastic filament with tension, shear and bending moment.
ideas.modern_name: Planar Kirchhoff rod / Euler–Bernoulli nonlinear dynamic rod equations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E410, 1771), as emphasised by Truesdell; Kirchhoff 1859 for 3D
ideas.where_published: E410; Truesdell 1960 analyses it as Euler's general equations for flexible and elastic bodies

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a routine resolution of d'Alembert inertial forces into tangent and normal components. E410's general equations are well known and were highlighted by Truesdell, so nothing appears unrecorded.
transcription_corrections: This page's transcription matches the image reasonably well; the I° and II° formulas are correctly bracketed.
Next page: 'quatuor aequationes ... (Vv = S(dΦ/dt))' should almost certainly be S(∂Φ/∂s) (bending moment proportional to curvature).
Next page: 'functionem esse ipsius S tantum' should read 'ipsius s tantum'.
